reason: E1 shows that longer sintering times at 1350 °C lead to copper evaporation and pore formation, supporting the premise that evaporation causes voids. However, neither E1 nor E2 directly tests an ultrafast, short-dwell SPS cycle at ~1280 °C with high pressure to suppress evaporation; E2 demonstrates property improvements via SPS with additives, not by curtailing evaporation through dwell-time reduction. The key mechanistic link between shortened dwell time and suppressed evaporation is not directly evidenced by the cited passages.
premises: Copper evaporation during liquid-phase sintering of W–Cu causes phase separation and interfacial voids
Shortening the sintering dwell time can suppress copper evaporation and void formation
High applied pressure during sintering enhances copper infiltration and densification
Reducing interfacial voids improves thermal conductivity of W–Cu composites
Ultrafast SPS (high pressure, ~10 min dwell near 1280 °C) can achieve these effects
